# Data-quality notes (generated by scripts/01_eda.py)

* Partitions: {'student_test': 10, 'train': 80} trips; each trip has its own `.track`, `.nodes`, `.arcs`, `.route` (all present).
* NaN values in raw tracks: 0; non-monotonic timestamps: 0 trips.
* Sampling: median interval 1 s, 96.7% of all steps are exactly 1 s. 23 trips have at least one gap > 60 s; largest gaps (train): 00000090: 153064 s, 00000078: 52810 s, 00000069: 2658 s.
* Trips are spread over several continents (see trip_locations.png), so every trip is projected to its own UTM zone; degree-based distances are never used.
* Road networks: 299-155003 nodes per trip, 95% (median) of arcs have a reverse twin (two-way streets) -> direction must be inferred from GPS heading.
* Isolated nodes total: 0; median weak components per trip: 19; invalid arcs: 0.
* Reference routes: all arc ids valid = True; consecutive route arcs connected (median trip) = 100.0%.
* The route gives the arc *sequence*, not a label per fix; labels per fix come from a monotonic alignment (src/pathsnap/labels.py). Fixes whose aligned distance exceeds 100 m are flagged unreliable and excluded from training and scoring (see label_alignment_*.csv).
* Trips with poor GPS/route agreement (median aligned distance): 00000054: 140 m, 00000033: 122 m, 00000043: 11 m - treated as reference-route limitations, not deleted.
